sanjay_customer: Hey — after yesterday's API key rotation ~15% of prod-eu requests to /v1/generate are returning 403 (invalid_api_key). Other pods are fine. No config changes besides the rotation. Anyone seen this pattern?

alicia_support: Sorry you're hitting this — can you paste a redacted request/response snippet and the rotation job id? Also which key id (kid) did you rotate to?

sanjay_customer: Request header: Authorization: Bearer sk_live_XXXXXXXX
Response: {"error":"unauthorized","code":403,"message":"invalid_api_key"}
Rotation CI job: rotate-service-key-2026-03-17-1402 (ran 2026-03-17T14:02Z)

alicia_support: thanks. On our side logs show some auth failures with "kid not found" and some with "signature mismatch". Can you confirm the client is sending the new key (and not an old cached token)? Any CDN or edge caching in front?

sanjay_customer: clients are direct to API (no CDN). We verified some pods are using new key (they show success) and a few still failing. I suspect some environment mismatch.

mike_infra: quick checks: 1) confirm Vault secret at secret/tenants/acme/service/api_key 2) check pod env var contents 3) check KMS alias/kid metadata if using rewrap. Commands: 
  vault kv get -field=api_key secret/tenants/acme/service
  kubectl exec -it <pod> -- /bin/sh -c 'printf "%s" "$REDWOOD_API_KEY" | od -An -t x1'
  kubectl describe secret acme-service-secret | grep -i creation

linda_devex: also check for trailing newline — CI pipelines often `echo "$KEY" > file` which appends a \n. That would change the key string and cause auth to fail for clients that trim vs those that don't. You can detect newline with `printf "%q" "$REDWOOD_API_KEY"` or the od command mike posted.

sanjay_customer: ran the od command on one of the failing pods: output shows `.. 6b 65 79 5f 6c 69 6e 65 0a` (ends with 0a). On a healthy pod it ends with `... 6b 65 79 5f 6c 69 6e 65` (no 0a). So looks like trailing newline present on the failing ones.

alicia_support: that explains the 403s — server treats the key bytewise so extra \n changes signature. Why are only some pods affected?

mike_infra: probable cause: Vault updated with new value (with newline) but many deployments read the secret into env at pod start. Kubernetes Secrets don't update env vars on running pods. If your Helm/Deployment didn't get a restart, pods keep older value. Also check if you have checksum annotations in your helm deployment that would trigger restart on secret change — if your release flow computed checksum before the Vault update, the annotation may not have changed.

sanjay_customer: Ah — our rotation job wrote new secret to Vault, then later updated the helm values, but the helm apply used values file that still had the old checksum (we compute checksum in the pipeline from a local file before we write to Vault). Looks like ordering race.

linda_devex: root cause summary: CI wrote secret with trailing newline (echo), Vault entry contains newline; deploy step that triggers rollout used a pre-rotation checksum so the checksum annotation stayed the same => some pods rolled (new value) while others stayed (old or with newline) depending on timing and restart policy.

alicia_support: mitigation for immediate fix: 1) trim the secret in Vault to remove trailing newline (use `vault kv put secret/tenants/acme/service api_key="$(printf \"%s\" \"$KEY\" )"`) or update via API ensuring no newline; 2) force a rollout restart of the deployments so all pods pick up the env: `kubectl rollout restart deploy/acme-service --namespace=prod` 3) verify pods' env with the od command.

mike_infra: we ran the commands with the customer (with their consent): trimmed secret and then `kubectl rollout restart` -> all pods now show no 0a and 0% 403s in the next 10 minutes.

sanjay_customer: confirmed — errors dropped to 0 over the next 12 minutes. Thanks! :relieved:

linda_devex: followups to prevent recurrence: 
- In CI, write secrets with `printf '%s' "$KEY" | vault kv put secret/... api_key=@-` or `echo -n` to avoid newline.
- Add a CI step that validates no trailing whitespace: `printf '%s' "$KEY" | od -An -t x1 | grep -q "0a" && fail`.
- Compute secret checksum after writing to Vault (not before) so Helm's checksum annotation changes and triggers rollout.
- Consider using the Kubernetes CSI Secrets Store or a sidecar that updates envs or restarts pods automatically on secret change.

alicia_support: note for support runbook: when seeing partial 403s after rotation, check (1) newline/trailing whitespace in secret (2) whether pods were restarted (checksum annotation mismatch) (3) KMS/JWK kid mapping mismatches. Add these to the rotation playbook.

sanjay_customer: adding: we updated pipeline already to `printf` and added the post-write checksum step. Appreciate the quick help, saved our weekend. :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: deploy/acme-service-prod v3.12.7 rolled at 2026-03-17T16:10Z (trigger: manual rollout-restart)

alicia_support: marking this resolved; will add to knowledge base. If anything resurfaces ping support with the rotation job id. :thumbsup:
